title: Introduce shared JOSE facade and zero-downtime crypto upgrades
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Multiple services embed ad-hoc JWT/SAML/JWS parsing code and link against varying OpenSSL and JOSE libraries. This has led to transitive dependency churn, occasional CVE mitigation delays, and hard-to-test crypto paths. Goal: create a lightweight, internal JOSE facade library (go/jose-facade) that centralizes JWT/JWS/OIDC operations, provides a stable API for SAML adapters to call, and allows coordinated OpenSSL/JOSE upgrades with zero-downtime migration.

Scope: facade library, KMS-backed signing/verification hooks, runtime feature flagging for old/new crypto path, separate process for SAML adapters to isolate XML dependencies, compatibility shim for OpenSSL 1.1 -> 3.x transitions, e2e test harness and perf benchmarks. Not in scope: migrating third-party customer SDKs (handled separately).

Success criteria: facade implemented with parity for current runtime use-cases; automated canary that routes 5% traffic -> new path for 2 days with no errors; no user-facing latency regression >5% p50; all relevant CVE fixes verified in our build matrix; security review signed off and rollout playbook added to runbooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New internal package 'internal/josefacade' compiles and is vendored in runtime and auth services.
2) KMS signing/verification introduced behind a feature flag.
3) SAML adapters forked to 'saml-adapter' process with isolated deps and health-checks.
4) Controlled rollout steps documented and validated in canary.
5) Automation added to CI to test OpenSSL 1.1 and OpenSSL 3 builds.
6) Security review completed and at least two engineers approved the changelist.
migration_plan:
- Phase 0 (Design): finalise facade API, list crypto operations, and map callers (week 1).
- Phase 1 (Build): implement josefacade with in-process shim + KMS provider, wire feature flag (week 2-3).
- Phase 2 (SAML isolation): extract SAML adapters to separate process and add RPC shim (week 3).
- Phase 3 (Canary): enable new path for 5% traffic for 48h, watch latency and error budget (week 4).
- Phase 4 (Rollout): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with autoscaling thresholds.
- Rollback: feature flag off + route drain + revert to previous signing provider if errors > threshold.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: subtle JWT/JWS verification differences could lead to token rejections. Mitigation: maintain a 'compat' mode that runs both old and new verifiers in parallel (compare outputs, only fail-open during canary).
Risk: SAML process boundary adds RPC latency. Mitigation: keep hot path cached and run perf microbenchmarks; add local vs remote path configuration.
Risk: OpenSSL ABI differences. Mitigation: build matrix in CI for both ABIs and provide an internal compatibility shim for symbols we depend on.
comments: 2026-02-22 — Asha Raman: Created ticket after spike with security. Identified repeated ad-hoc JOSE parsers and two SAML adapters that pull in xmlsec. Proposal: single facade + isolate SAML. Asked for architecture review and dependencies list.

2026-02-25 — Liam O'Connor: Architecture review notes attached. Decided on pluggable KMS provider (local dev signer + cloud KMS in prod). Chose to implement 'compare-mode' to run old and new verifiers in parallel during canary. Action: PR for facade interface by end of week.

2026-02-28 — Security (Maya Chen): Requested threat model addendum focusing on key usage, key rotation, and audit log surface area. Also asked for a plan to prove no downgrade attacks between old/new paths.

2026-03-03 — Liam O'Connor: First cut of internal/josefacade landed in feature branch. Basic sign/verify + jwk cache implemented. Local tests show parity for the 8 canonical token shapes we have. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284. Noted one flaky test around header ordering — added to flaky-tests board.

2026-03-05 — QA (Sora Patel): Integration harness run against staging with OpenSSL 1.1 and 3.0 variants. Observed 1.7% median latency increase on verification when running via the RPC shim; in-process path shows <0.5% impact. Recommendation: keep SAML adapters co-located for initial rollout and move to process boundary in a later phase if needed.

2026-03-08 — Security (Maya Chen): Preliminary review pass. Asked to ensure key rotation tests and audit logging are present in CI. Also requested that any third-party xmlsec usage be constrained to sandboxed process and chroot where possible.
Action: Liam to add rotation tests and hardened SAML container baseline.

2026-03-10 — Liam O'Connor: Canary plan drafted. Steps include: enable feature flag for 5% traffic, compare-mode enabled for 72 hours, automatic alerting on token verification discordance, rollback triggers (>0.1% user-facing 5xx or >2x variance in p95). Added runbook link: docs/runbooks/crypto-upgrade-playbook.md.
PRs: runtime#1284 (facade), auth-service#402 (KMS integration).
2026-03-11 — Asha Raman: Provided review feedback on facade API: prefer declarative signer config and explicit algorithm whitelisting. Approved moving to canary once rotation tests land.
next_steps:
1) Add key rotation unit/integration tests to CI (owner: Liam).
2) Harden SAML container baseline and add monitoring (owner: Infra team).
3) Schedule canary for staging window 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-17.
4) Security review sign-off and tabletop exercise before canary start.
notes: This ticket ties into larger dependency hygiene work — aim is to reduce the number of places we link directly to xmlsec/OpenSSL and instead centralize crypto responsibilities. Keep changes minimal on hot path and prefer opt-in via feature flags until metrics are stable.
